newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss machinery sector orders fall 3.7 pct in q1.
newsitem.headline: Swiss machinery sector orders fall 3.7 pct in q1.

text.p: Orders received by Swiss machinery companies fell 3.7 percent in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the year-earlier period, two industry groups said, but they expressed guarded optimism for the year as a whole.

Data from the VSM and ASM industry associations showed foreign orders fell 2.6 percent in the quarter, an improvement from the 14.6 percent slide in the fourth quarter of 1996. Domestic orders dropped 13.5 percent.
Turnover also fell 3.7 percent in the quarter, with foreign sales rising five percent when expressed in the weak Swiss franc and domestic turnover down 15.3 percent.
Exports rose 1.6 percent in nominal terms in the first quarter, but exports to the EU slipped by one percent.

"For the current year, the VSM still expects a slow improvement in a tough situation," it said, noting restrained growth in western Europe and the weaker franc should create better business conditions in the second half of the year.
A successful conclusion of bilateral negotiations with the EU on closer economic ties would also send a positive signal, it said.
